claims: A mortgage broker acts as an intermediary between homebuyers and lenders.
Mortgage brokers shop across multiple institutions to find the best rates and loan options for borrowers.
Mortgage brokers are generally paid a commission by the lender often 1% to 2% of the loan principal only after the loan closes.
The most common scenario is that the lender pays the mortgage broker a commission upon closing.
Occasionally the borrower pays the mortgage broker directly.
Occasionally the broker fee is rolled into the loan amount.
The Truth in Lending Act prohibits brokers from collecting fees from both the lender and borrower.
Some lenders only work directly with customers and do not use brokers.
Mortgage broker licensing typically involves pre-licensing education courses.
Mortgage broker licensing typically involves passing a written exam.
Mortgage broker licensing typically involves background checks.
Mortgage broker licensing typically involves continuing education for license renewal.
A broker connects homebuyers with multiple lenders to find the best option.
A lender is a bank or financial institution that lends its own money directly.
